key_distinction: REGISTRATION is what this measures: a coast-band warp is a non-rigid registration of the DM chart to the atlas print coast. The RENDERING MEDIUM does not change any number here; a vector city carried through the same warp bends exactly as the raster does, and a vector city placed through cityBox misaligns exactly as the raster does.

method.inputs: HEAD export only. Print = numpy port of buildCityMask on PIL-decoded z5 tiles (maps-site/tiles/5) over window [1060,1860)x[1240,2040) +20 px pad, islets < 400 atlas px2 filled (the pw mask the dm_art_placements rows of three-coasts-epeshu.json use). Chart = maps-site/art/overlay-Epeshu.jpg 2863x3072, water class L1 distance to RGB(119,153,136) < 36 and nearer than olive RGB(102,119,85), opened 2x, largest component, holes filled (exact-fill pixels 15.5%, class 16.1%). Chart coast points: pixel edges >40 art px from the frame, every 4th (972 points), as in three-coasts.
method.placement: cityBox as worldPOICoord/cityBox do: capital FOOT_R 26, hw=26*2863/3072=24.23, hh=26, times scale s, centre (1236.1+E, 1415). atlas px per chart px = 0.016927 (1.0x), 0.013542 (0.8x), 0.010156 (0.6x).
method.vectors: One-sided: each chart coast point c_i (atlas px) gets d_i = nearest print coast point - c_i (cKDTree over the whole window print coast). No vector exceeded 30 atlas px, so none was capped.
method.field: u(x) = [sum_i w_i d_i / sum_i w_i] * g(t). w_i = exp(-|x-c_i|^2/(2*2^2)) (Nadaraya-Watson along-shore smoothing, sigma 2 atlas px). t = distance from x to the chart shoreline (full-resolution chart coast, unsigned, so the same decay applies inland and seaward). g = radial Gaussian taper, sigma R/2, renormalised to 1 at t=0 and 0 at t=R, zero beyond: g(t)=(exp(-t^2/(2(R/2)^2))-e^-2)/(1-e^-2). R = 6 or 12 atlas px. Evaluated on an 8 chart px node grid (0.08-0.14 atlas px), bilinear between nodes. max|g'| = 1.403/R, so a pure normal displacement folds (det<=0) once it exceeds R/1.403 = 4.28 (R6) or 8.55 (R12) atlas px.
method.raster_model: The delivered warp is a pre-warped plate. Primary rendering: land-wins forward splat, the mesh-warp model in which the chart's flat sea is painted first and the land drawn over it. Every chart pixel centre is pushed through T(x)=x+u(x); an output cell is land if any land pixel lands in it, else sea if any sea pixel does; remaining cells take a converged fixed-point backward preimage when one lies inside the frame, else they are plate_gap_no_source (the warped plate no longer covers that part of its own box). Contrast row seam_vs_print_naive_backward_atlas_px2: plain backward sampling, x <- y - u(x) for 60 iterations, which picks arbitrary preimages where the field folds.
method.metrics: Same keys as three-coasts-epeshu.json dm_art_placements. vs_print.art_to_print: warped chart coast, taken as edges between land-hit and sea-hit cells of a 2 chart px output lattice, every 2nd edge, frame margin 40, against all print coast points. print_to_art_in_box: print coast points inside the box (shrunk 1 px) against the warped chart coast. seam_vs_print_atlas_px2: 0.25 atlas px grid over [1211,1389]-[1269,1441], cell 0.0625 px2. vs_print_forward_points: T(c_i) against the print, the warp's own target fit. Displacement and Jacobian are taken over the node grid (equal-area samples); land and sea are chart classes. A u=0 control on the 2 px lattice reproduces the 1 px baseline to within 0.04 px rms (raster_lattice_control_u0).
method.wall_ring: The chart's wall ring is not in any data file, so it was traced by eye from overlay-Epeshu.jpg: a thick slate line with tower nodes running from the north-west shore (873,773) east round the Marble Quarter and the Forum to the south-west shore (107,2318), with Outwall (POI 11) outside it. There are 21 vertices (wall_ring_vertices_art_px), accurate to about 15 chart px, densified to 5 px. Its two ends sit on the shore by construction. Per case the file reports displacement along the wall, segment strain (|len_after/len_before - 1| over 5 px segments), segment turn (the change in direction after warping) and the minimum det.
method.pois: maps-site/data/chart-pois.json Epēshu (19). worldPOICoord maps p.x/poiRef.w*box.fw with poiRef = DETAIL['Epēshu'] = 3914x4200 (detail-charts.json). That box is the same aspect as the 2863x3072 art, so chart px = p.x*2863/3914, p.y*3072/4200. Displacement is sampled at those chart px.
method.scripts: Throwaway numpy/scipy scripts in a mktemp dir (base.py, warp.py, viz2.py, write.py). Nothing under the repo or maps-site/ was written.

pre_warped_plate.new_raster_bytes: A re-encoded maps-site/art/overlay-Epeshu.jpg. HEAD holds 2,171,695 B, and a re-encode at similar quality is of the same order (not encoded here). The A-U11 preview art/overlay-Epeshu-720.jpg must be regenerated too. Chart mode (enterChart) reads the separate pyramid charts/epeshu (370 files, 6.6 MB in HEAD); it keeps the unwarped geometry unless that pyramid is re-cut as well.
pre_warped_plate.tiles_v: TILES_V is one global (maps-site/index.html: var TILES_V=1; function tv(u)). tv() and the ?t= suffix version every raster under tiles/, tiles-war/, tiles-imperial/, charts/ and art/: 3,364 files and about 36.7 MB in HEAD. A bump to ship one warped plate changes the URL of all of them, so every returning device refetches any raster it views, and once D7 is in, the worker cache atlas-raster-t<TILES_V> is replaced. tools/build-offline-manifest.js --check exits 1 if a listed raster changed while TILES_V did not, and the manifest must be regenerated with --atlas.
pre_warped_plate.a_u11_conflict: A-U11 acceptance: "after load the full image is the same file and the final shot equals R1 at max zoom; registerCityOverlay literal kept". A warped plate is a different file with a different final shot. That is the ruling that rejected the pre-feathered plate (gap-mobile:C10).
pre_warped_plate.poi_consequence: worldPOICoord and buildWorldPOIs place the 19 POIs linearly in cityBox (box.x0+p.x/pr.w*box.fw). After the warp, the art under 7 to 10 of the 16 land POIs moves by more than 1 atlas px (up to 3.5 px at 0.6x+3E and 6.9 px at 1.0x R12, which is 207 / 408 screen px at z9.885). The markers would then sit off their quarters unless the same displacement field also ships as data and is applied in JS.
pre_warped_plate.pins: The field is offline data, so determinism is untouched. The mobile pins (xmur3, mulberry32, genCityCanvas, washMake, sampleCityMask, cityCanvasSha) cover the procedural path, not the canon Epēshu plate, so the pins themselves are not hit. The A-U11 same-file rule and the TILES_V/manifest gates are hit.

runtime_css_clip_fill.tiles_v: no bump; overlay-Epeshu.jpg, its 720 px preview and charts/epeshu stay byte-identical; A-U11 same-file rule holds (gap-mobile:C10: the CSS-mask variant does not conflict)
runtime_css_clip_fill.covers: A clip against atlas water removes land-over-sea, which is what remains after the warp too (70-79 px2 at 0.6x+3E). Sea-over-land (75.3 px2 unwarped at 0.6x+3E, 28.6 px2 warped) needs a land fill or an opaque base under the plate in both cases, because the base sits at 0.12 at z>=8.

delivery_cost.runtime_mesh_warp: A canvas or WebGL mesh warp of the unchanged plate would also cost no raster bytes, but it was not measured: no browser was run. It inherits every fabric number in coast_warp (the bending is a property of the field, not of where the warp runs), and it needs the field as data plus the same displacement applied to the POI markers.

verdicts.seam: The warp shrinks the chart-to-print residual at the chart's own shoreline but does not close the seam. At 0.6x+3E, art_to_print goes from 3.58/6.66 to 1.72/3.60 (R6) and 1.69/3.19 (R12). Land-over-sea goes from 91.1 to 78.5 / 70.5 px2, and sea-over-land from 75.3 to 28.6 px2. The print coast inside the box stays poorly matched: print_to_art_in_box rms goes only from 5.30 to 4.64, p95 8.55, max 9.24. The one-sided chart-to-print vectors can only move the shoreline the chart already has. Print water with no chart counterpart stays under chart land: the harbour lobe north-east of the chart coast at the top of the box, and the bay south of where the chart coast leaves the box. Today (1.0x) land-over-sea goes from 666.5 to 471.2 (R6) and 387.7 (R12).
verdicts.third_sign: The warp adds a third seam sign. Where the coast crosses the plate frame, the frame is displaced (max 5.9 atlas px at 0.6x, 12.4 at 0.8x, 20.3 at 1.0x), so the warped plate no longer covers 49 to 67 px2 (0.6x), 107 to 182 (0.8x) or 183 to 369 (1.0x) of its own box. Almost all of that area (>=95%) is print sea. Left open, it shows the base at 0.12, and the total misregistered area at 0.6x+3E is 156.2 / 165.8 px2 against 166.4 unwarped: no net gain. Padded with the flat sea fill when pre-warping, the total is 107.3 / 102.5 px2, a 36-38% cut that still leaves both signs.
verdicts.fabric: The city fabric bends. At 0.6x+3E there are no folds on land (det min 0.11), but the old harbour quarters are strongly re-proportioned. Wood Quay (POI 2) moves 346 chart px (3.5 atlas px) with det 2.92 (R6), and Necropolis (1), Marble Quarter (4) and Māmban (8) move 2.3 to 3.3 atlas px. The wall ring moves up to 216 chart px (2.2 atlas px; 62% of its length moves more than 2 chart px) with segment strain up to 52.7% and turns up to 12.7 deg (R12: 292 chart px, 99.4% of its length, strain 54.4%). At 1.0x (DM scale) R6 tears the city: 3.6% of chart land folds (76 atlas px2, det min -2.5) and wall segments turn 139 deg. R12 still folds 0.31% of land and moves the wall 451 chart px (7.6 atlas px). That is above the analytic fold threshold for an inward move, R/1.403 = 4.28 / 8.55 atlas px, against the 9.6 px max landward one-sided vector at 1.0x.
verdicts.pct_moved: The % of chart area moved more than 2 chart px is 23-60% across the cases. 2 chart px is only 0.020-0.034 atlas px, so the land share moved more than 1 atlas px is the more telling figure: 9.5-23%.
verdicts.dm_scale: A coast-band warp cannot keep the DM's scale. At 1.0x it needs moves up to 20 atlas px, folds land at R6 and R12, and still leaves 388-471 px2 of land over sea. The scale still has to be chosen by policy (0.6x+3E stays best) and cannot come from the coast.
verdicts.recommended_class: The recommended class does not change: a policy translate+scale per-city override, plus a runtime CSS clip against atlas water, plus a land fill or opaque base for the sea-over-land band. That class costs zero raster bytes. A pre-warped plate would trim the residual further but needs a TILES_V bump that refetches every raster (3,364 files, about 36.7 MB), conflicts with A-U11's same-file rule, and must carry its field into worldPOICoord. All that buys 36-38% less misregistered area while bending the wall and the harbour quarters.
verdicts.caveats: The parameters are this prototype's own choices: along-shore sigma 2 atlas px, taper sigma R/2, one-sided nearest vectors with no regularisation. A two-sided or landmark-matched field might close more of the seam, but it would bend the fabric at least as much, since the print water it would have to open lies inside today's chart land. Print and chart masks are PIL decodes, not browser decodes. The wall ring was traced by eye (about 15 chart px accurate). Its ends touch the shore by construction, so its maximum displacement is at its ends.
verdicts.radius: R6 and R12 give identical shoreline numbers in every placement (vs_print_forward_points; sea_over_land 28.6/28.6 and print_to_art_in_box 4.64/4.64 at 0.6x+3E). That follows from the construction: g(0)=1, so the shoreline lands in the same place whatever R is. R is a fabric knob, setting how far inland the bend reaches (land POIs moved >1 atlas px: 7 vs 9; wall moved >2 chart px: 62% vs 99% at 0.6x+3E). It is not a seam knob. Seam closure is set by the one-sided vectors and by sigma_s, and no decay radius closes the seam.
